newsitem.title: UK: By-election voters fire warning shot at UK Labour.
newsitem.headline: By-election voters fire warning shot at UK Labour.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party was licking its wounds on Friday after losing to the Conservative opposition in the first test of voter opinion since Labour swept to power in the May 1 general election.
Conservative candidate John Randall secured a five percent swing away from Labour to retain the seat of Uxbridge, west London, in a parliamentary by-election.
Randall's majority of 3,766 was almost five times the 724-vote margin secured by Sir Michael Shersby in May. The by-election was prompted by Shersby's death.

Conservative Party chairman Lord Cecil Parkinson hailed the result as a triumph for William Hague, who replaced ex-prime minister John Major as party leader after Labour's landslide general election victory ended 18 years of Conservative rule.
Hague was due to attend a party celebration in Uxbridge later on Friday -- at a bar called "The Turning Point".
"He will be pleased. I think he has a right to be," Parkinson told BBC radio.
